search_row.title: War of attrition ESS
search_row.statement: In contests settled by display, where the animal willing to persist longer wins and costs grow with time, the stable strategy is to choose a persistence time at random from an exponential distribution whose mean equals the resource value.
search_row.math: with cost linear in time at unit rate and resource value V, the ESS persistence time has density p(x) = \frac{1}{V} e^{-x/V}

fields.dct:source: John Maynard Smith (1974) The theory of games and the evolution of animal conflicts
fields.delphi:proposedTest: Record contest durations in a display-based contest system and test for an exponential distribution, with the mean scaling with experimentally varied resource value.
fields.delphi:context: Assumptions: symmetric contests, cost linear in display time, no information about the opponent's choice. Formal status: proved (Maynard Smith 1974); existence and uniqueness in the generalized game proved by Bishop and Cannings (1978).
fields.skos:notation: with cost linear in time at unit rate and resource value V, the ESS persistence time has density p(x) = \frac{1}{V} e^{-x/V}
fields.dct:description: In contests settled by display, where the animal willing to persist longer wins and costs grow with time, the stable strategy is to choose a persistence time at random from an exponential distribution whose mean equals the resource value.
